title: CLI Tools
concept: Building professional CLI tools with XIOM — argument parsing, colored output, progress bars, and interactive terminal interfaces.
why: CLI tools are the backbone of developer workflows. XIOM's fast startup, small binaries, and cross-compilation make it perfect for CLI applications.
syntax_ref:
use xiom.cli;     // Argument parsing
use xiom.term;    // Terminal colors and styles
use xiom.progress; // Progress bars and spinners
use xiom.dialog;  // Interactive prompts
use xiom.table;   // Formatted tables

fn main() -> Int { /* return 0 on success */ }
tips: Always support --help and --version — it's the first thing users try
Use exit codes: 0 = success, non-zero = error (1 = general error, 2 = misuse, etc.)
Detect whether stdout is a terminal before using colors/progress bars (piped output should be plain)
Fast startup is critical for CLI tools — optimize cold start time over runtime performance
common_mistakes: Writing to stdout for errors — use stderr for error messages and diagnostics
Assuming terminal width is 80 columns — detect and adapt with term::width()
Blocking without feedback — always show a spinner or progress for operations > 1 second
